info.name: Movie Ticket Booking System
info.description:
Every endpoint of the movie ticket booking backend, in the order you'd use them: set up the catalog, price it,
schedule a show, browse, book, pay, cancel, and finally cancel the show.

**Run the whole collection** (Collection Runner, or `npx newman run`) against an empty or used database: each
request saves the ids the next ones need, every name gets a per-run suffix, and every request has tests.
Requests can also be sent one by one, top to bottom.

Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:8080`). User ids are generated on the first request.

Amounts are in **paise** (₹1 = 100 paise). Times are ISO-8601 with an offset. Errors are RFC 9457
`application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. See `docs/USAGE.md` for the full guide.

item.name: 0. Before you start
item.description:
Shows what every request needs. The gateway in front of this service authenticates callers and forwards who they
are as headers; here you set them yourself:

| Header | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `X-User-Id` | yes | a UUID |
| `X-User-Role` | yes | `ADMIN` or `CUSTOMER` |
| `X-User-Name`, `X-User-Email`, `X-User-Phone` | no | stored so emails and SMS can reach the customer |

`/api/v1/admin/**` is for admins only.

request.description: Without `X-User-Id` (or with an invalid one) every `/api/v1/**` call is `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.

exec: // fresh names, ids and dates on every run, so the collection can be run again on the same database

request.description: Admin endpoints reject customers with `403 FORBIDDEN`.

item.name: 1. Catalog (admin)
item.description:
Cities, theaters, screens, seat layouts and movies: the things shows are scheduled on. Nothing is ever hard-deleted;
`deactivate` hides a row from customers and from new shows while keeping history intact.

request.description:
Creates a city. `timezone` is optional and defaults to `Asia/Kolkata`; show times are listed in it.

Names are unique (`409 ALREADY_EXISTS`).
Renames a city or changes its state or timezone.
The city picker: every active city.
A theater belongs to one city for life (the city can't be changed later).
Name, area and address.
Screens get a seat layout next; a screen without an active layout can't host shows.
Renames a screen.
One theater, including its screens.
The theater's price per seat category, **in paise** (30000 = ₹300). New shows copy these; a show can override them.
Prices by category code.

Describes the seat grid row by row. Each row is a list of segments: a run of seats (`from`–`to`, with a category) or an `aisle` gap of N columns. `blocked` seats are never sold (a pillar); `wheelchair` seats are marked as such.

A new layout starts as a DRAFT.
Only a DRAFT can be edited. Once active, a layout never changes: shows keep the version they were created on, and the next change is a new draft.
Makes the draft the screen's ACTIVE layout; the previous active one is RETIRED. New shows on the screen use it.

item.name: All layout versions of the screen

request.description: Every version, newest first, with its status.
`durationMin` sets how long the screen is taken by each show (plus a 20-minute cleaning buffer).
Existing shows keep their times; only new shows use the new duration.
Title, duration, certification and release date.

item.name: 2. Pricing and refund policies (admin)
item.description:
What a seat costs: the show's category price, then day-of-week rules, then a coupon discount, then a convenience
fee (₹20 a seat) and 18% GST on the ticket and on the fee. What comes back on cancellation is set by the refund
policy the booking was sold under.

request.description: Includes the seeded global `Weekend +20%` rule.

A day-of-week surcharge. `scopeType` is GLOBAL, CITY or THEATER (with `scopeId`); when several match, the most specific wins. `daysOfWeek` uses 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday. `adjustmentType` PERCENT adds a percentage of the tier price, FLAT adds paise per seat; `adjustmentValue` is always positive. `validFrom` / `validTo` (dates, optional) limit when it applies.
`active: false` keeps the rule but stops applying it.
Holds already priced keep their price.

`discountType` FLAT (paise) or PERCENT (with an optional `maxDiscountPaise`). `minOrderPaise` is checked against the order before the discount. `maxUses` caps total uses (empty = unlimited) and `perUserLimit` uses per customer. `scopes` limits where it works (CITY, THEATER, MOVIE or seat CATEGORY); empty means everywhere. Codes are 3–30 letters and digits and can't change later.
Every coupon, newest first, with `usedCount`.
Same body as create, without `code`. `maxUses` can't go below the uses already made.
`Standard` is the default out of the box: 100% of the ticket price 24h+ before the show, 50% from 4h, nothing after; fees kept.

`type` SLAB (percent by hours before the show), FULL (everything back) or NON_REFUNDABLE (the customer can still cancel to free the seats, but gets nothing). Slab percentages can't grow as the show gets closer. `refundFees` (SLAB only) also returns the convenience fee.
A policy with its slabs, most hours first.
Only affects bookings confirmed from now on: each booking keeps a copy of the terms it was sold under.
The default applies to shows that don't name their own policy.
Puts things back the way they were.

item.name: 3. Shows (admin)
item.description:
A show is a movie on a screen at a time. It's created SCHEDULED, opened for sale, and may be cancelled. Creating one
copies the screen's active layout into per-show seats and the theater's prices into per-show prices.

request.description:
`startTime` carries its offset. `showDate` (optional) is the listing date; shows before 03:00 are listed under the previous day by default. `priceOverrides` (optional) replaces the theater's price for some categories. `refundPolicyId` (optional) picks this show's refund policy; otherwise the default applies.

The screen is taken from start to end plus a 20-minute cleaning buffer.
A database exclusion constraint keeps two shows from overlapping on one screen, even when two admins try at the same moment.

item.name: Change prices for this show only

request.description: Paise by category code. Holds already made keep the price they were quoted.
Only OPEN shows are listed to customers and can be booked, until 10 minutes before the start.

item.name: A theater's shows for a date

request.description: The admin schedule view.

item.name: 4. Browse (customer)
item.description:
The customer's path to a seat: city → movie → date → theater and time → seat map. Listings are cached in Redis
for a minute; the seat map and seats-left counts are always live.

request.description: Movies with at least one open show in the next 7 days.
The dates in the next 7 days on which the movie has an open show in the city.
Theaters showing the movie on that date, each with its showtimes, lowest price, seats left and an availability badge (AVAILABLE, FILLING_FAST, SOLD_OUT).
`slot` is any of MORNING, AFTERNOON, EVENING, NIGHT (combined with OR); `language` and `format` narrow further.
Every seat with its label, grid position, category, type and live status: AVAILABLE, HELD, BOOKED or BLOCKED. Category prices here include the day's adjustment but not fees or GST.

exec: const id = label => seats.find(s => s.label === label).seatId;
pm.test('A5 is blocked by the layout', () => pm.expect(seats.find(s => s.label === 'A5').status).to.eql('BLOCKED'));

item.name: 5. Book and pay (customer)
item.description:
A hold claims seats for 8 minutes at a frozen price. Paying confirms it; a declined payment gives the seats back;
a slow payment answers 202 and finishes in the background.

`POST` requests that change money or seats take an `Idempotency-Key` header (a UUID the client makes per action).
Sending the same key again returns the first answer instead of doing the work twice.

request.description: Claims every requested seat or none of them (up to 10). The response has the price per seat and in total, and `holdExpiresAt` for the countdown. `couponCode` is optional.
Same `Idempotency-Key`, same body: the first answer is replayed and no second booking is made. The same key with a different body is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

item.name: Someone else wants the same seat → 409

request.description: Every seat is sold exactly once, however many people click at the same moment.

item.name: A second hold on the same show → 409

request.description: One live hold per customer and show; finish or release the first.
Re-prices the hold without a discount and gives the coupon use back. Seats and expiry don't change.
Checks the coupon (validity, scope, minimum order, limits) and re-prices the hold. An unusable coupon is `422 COUPON_INVALID` with the reason.
Details of one of your bookings. Someone else's booking is `404`, never `403`, so ids don't leak.

Pays for the hold. `details.type` is CARD, UPI, NET_BANKING or WALLET. The gateway is simulated: `simulate` is SUCCESS (default), FAILURE or DELAYED.

200 with `paymentStatus` SUCCESS → the booking is CONFIRMED, the seats BOOKED and a confirmation email sent. 200 with FAILED → the booking is FAILED and the seats free again. 202 PENDING → see the delayed example below. Starting to pay keeps the seats at least 5 more minutes.
A confirmed booking can't be paid twice (a retry with the *same* key would replay the first answer instead).
Letting a hold go frees its seats and coupon at once.
`simulate: FAILURE`: a normal 200 with `paymentStatus: FAILED`; the booking is FAILED and the seats go straight back. Card numbers must pass the Luhn check (4242 4242 4242 4242 does).
`simulate: DELAYED`: `202 Accepted` with `paymentStatus: PENDING`; the booking stays PAYMENT_PENDING and the outcome arrives about 15 seconds later in the background. Poll `GET /bookings/{id}`.
`bankCode` is one of the configured banks (HDFC, ICICI, SBI, AXIS, KOTAK).

item.name: 6. Cancel and refund (customer)
item.description:
A confirmed booking can be cancelled in full or seat by seat until 30 minutes before the show. The refund follows
the policy the booking was sold under; the preview and the real cancellation always agree to the paisa.

request.description: What cancelling these seats now would refund; changes nothing. Leave `seatIds` out for every active seat. Inside the last 30 minutes it's `422 CANCELLATION_CLOSED`.

Cancels the seats (all active ones when `seatIds` is left out), frees them for sale and starts the refund. The booking stays CONFIRMED while seats remain, and the coupon is only given back once none do. `refundId` is null when nothing is refunded.
Each seat can be cancelled once.

`view` is UPCOMING (confirmed, show ahead), PAST (confirmed, show started) or CANCELLED. Pages start at 0; `size` is 1–50. Each item has the movie, theater, time, seats still booked and cancelled seats.
Seats with their status, every cancellation, and the payment with each refund's status (INITIATED → COMPLETED).

item.name: 7. An admin cancels the show
item.description:
Cancelling a show releases every hold and refunds every confirmed booking in full, fees included, in the background.
A payment still pending when it happens is refunded as soon as it lands.

request.description: Takes seats off sale for this show (a broken seat). The response lists seats it couldn't block (already sold, held or blocked).
Puts blocked seats back on sale.
The show disappears from browse at once; releases and refunds follow within seconds.
The remaining seat is cancelled with reason SHOW_CANCELLED and a 100% refund.

If Kabir's delayed payment landed after the show was cancelled (the usual case in a collection run), the booking is EXPIRED and the money refunded automatically with reason LATE_PAYMENT. If it landed first, the show cancellation refunded it (CANCELLED, SHOW_CANCELLED). Either way nobody keeps a paid seat on a cancelled show. This request waits ~16 seconds first.
The CANCELLED view of the history.

item.name: 8. Retire things (admin)
item.description: Deactivating hides a coupon, movie, screen, theater or city from customers and from new shows. History stays.

request.description: No new holds can use it.
No new shows can be scheduled for it.
No new shows on this screen.
Hides the theater and its screens.
Removes the city from the city picker.
